scope: Independent composition review of current V2 source and an original V3 blueprint. No transcription of the referenced song.

evidence.limits: Source-code/music-structure review only. Do not treat this document as evidence of listening to the KEXP audio or of perceptual improvement.

diagnosis.problem: The main arpeggio is an uninterrupted eight-note ladder in every bar.
diagnosis.evidence: left uses eight equally spaced notes in each of four rows; it remains active in all 36 bars.
diagnosis.consequence: Changing samples preserves a sequencer-like motor. There is no phrase breath or memorable rhythm cell.

diagnosis.evidence: The full sections stack left, right, chords, and lead concurrently.
diagnosis.consequence: A four-part guitar texture obscures a single singable theme; it is denser than a clear two-guitar conversation.

diagnosis.problem: The supposed human offset is a fixed musical displacement.
diagnosis.evidence: right.late(1/16) at 132 BPM equals about 114 ms.
diagnosis.consequence: This creates a systematic syncopation, not varied picking microtiming. Retain only if musically intentional.

diagnosis.problem: Rhythmic changes are mostly instrumentation swaps.
diagnosis.evidence: The same kick/snare ostinato is reused; hats keep eight eighths; lastOf(4) only adds two ghost hits; full sections repeat identically.
diagnosis.consequence: More layers and louder cymbals do not create math-rock phrase development.

diagnosis.problem: A four-bar harmony loop underlies every section.
diagnosis.evidence: D/F#/G/A root loop and same four-bar lead recur unchanged.
diagnosis.consequence: Neither the melody nor harmony changes direction at the second climax.

diagnosis.evidence: Fixed clip/attack/release values per guitar, long shared tails, no slide/late vibrato or string-aware damping.
diagnosis.consequence: Repeated long overlap and homogeneous attacks expose sample playback despite real recordings.

direction.coreRule: One foreground melodic guitar. The second guitar answers in its rests or plays a sparse rhythmic voicing; never add an unrelated third lead line.
direction.melodyRule: Repeat an identifiable rhythm and first few notes, then alter the destination and phrase ending. At least one sustained note and one deliberate rest per two-bar phrase.
direction.mathRule: Use displaced accents, interlocking rests and one short odd-meter passage. A clear 4/4 hook must remain the anchor.

A.name: Question and answer
A.intent: A singable pickup, step down, leap into a high target, then a slower answer. This is a newly composed phrase; it is not extracted from the reference.

support.accompanimentRule: During the held B4/A4/E4, one low two- or three-note voicing is enough. During the lead rest, give the second guitar a 2-note response. Do not keep the V2 continuous eighth-note ladder underneath.

A.development: On the second hook, keep the question prefix but delay one entry by an eighth; let the answer rise to D5 once, then resolve lower. Preserve recognition.

B.name: Interlocking short-long cells
B.intent: A contrasting instrumental figure. The rests belong to the groove; do not fill every rest with delay repeats.
B.adaptation7of8: Remove the final eighth-note slot, keep the first 7 eighths at the same tempo. Do not squeeze a 4/4 phrase into 7/8. Let the next bar arrive one eighth early.
B.adaptation5of8: Use a single 3+2 connecting bar: strong low dyad at 0, short reply at .5, rest at 1, two-note pickup at 1.5 and 2.

form.name: intro
form.material: Sparse B fragments; reveal its accents. Bass pickup only in the final bar.

form.name: theme_A
form.material: A question / answer, then repeat with a different final target. Two-guitar conversation, closed-hat groove.

form.name: turn
form.material: 7/8, group 2+2+3. A short stop then a pickup, not a random drum roll.

form.name: interlock_B
form.material: B in alternating 7/8 and 4/4; drums follow group heads, melody guitar yields to the interlock.

form.name: reset
form.material: 5/8, group 3+2. Leave the middle eighth empty and use the final two as a pickup.

form.name: theme_C
form.material: Return to A, wider but not uniformly higher; one sustained D5 at the phrase summit. Stronger backbeat, sparse open hats.

form.name: breath
form.material: Half-time feel. One guitar rings, the other is silent; bass moves only on harmonic changes.

form.name: final_C
form.material: Recognizable A with a changed answer and one displaced accent. Last two bars thin out instead of adding every layer.

form.name: outro
form.material: A short answer in a lower register and a final dyad. Stop new attacks and let real tails decay.

drums.timingUnit: quarter notes; onset values relative to each bar
rules: Bass attacks share selected kick positions, not every guitar note.
Do not play closed and open hats at the same instant.
Sparse crash only on a major return; omit it on repeat 2 to keep development.
Ghost-note sample is quieter than full backbeat; not simply the same sample at equal velocity.
Keep the triplet/two-sixteenth fill confined to a phrase boundary.

performance.slide: Use only at 2–4 chosen phrase targets per 8 bars; approach by 1–2 semitones over about 50–90 ms. Do not sweep every note.
performance.vibrato: Only on sustained notes; begin roughly 180–250 ms after the pluck. Start shallow, about 6–12 cents, 4.3–5.2 Hz. No continuous oscillator on short eighths.
performance.picking: Accent phrase heads, lighter passing notes, sparse hammer-like notes with a softened attack; alternate pick recordings without resetting the exact RR order every bar.
performance.muting: Use short damped articulations for rhythmic dyads; let open strings ring only where a player could hold them. A new note on the same string damps the previous note.
performance.microtiming: Keep the score grid exact. Apply correlated small offsets: snare about 3–8 ms late, hats within roughly ±4 ms, bass near selected kick attacks. Never randomize the whole ensemble independently by tens of ms.
performance.density: During the main melody, at most one other guitar role. Do not stack four unrelated guitar parts as in V2.

iterationGates: Render hook alone with bass/drums and no decoration: the 4-note prefix and question/answer must remain recognizable.
Compare dry guitar against processed guitar at matched level. Reject long delays that refill intentional rests.
Audit actual event durations and bar lengths, not only a time-signature label: 7/8 must be 3.5 quarters, 5/8 2.5 quarters.
Count distinct kick/snare patterns and phrase endings; section labels with identical event timings are not rhythmic development.
Check actual slide trajectory and vibrato start time in render; presence of a parameter alone is insufficient.
For tonal judgment, explicitly distinguish model/source analysis from genuinely auditioned audio. Do not claim a listening pass from a nonzero RMS test.
